headline: Local Trader Confirms Global Oil Prices Are Actually Regulated by His Neighborhood Chai Stall’s Coffee-Stirring Frequency
body:
Q: Mr. Sharma, the global markets have been volatile lately due to supply concerns, yet you claim the answer lies at your tea stall in South Delhi. How so?

A: It is quite simple, really. Whenever the supply concerns grow, I increase the speed at which I stir the coffee for my regular patrons. The vibrations travel through the pavement, directly impacting the oil futures desks in London and New York. If I stir clockwise, the barrel price dips; counter-clockwise, and it climbs.

Q: Are you suggesting the entire global petroleum market is dependent on your choice of beverage preparation?

A: Of course. Yesterday, when I ran out of milk and had to serve plain black tea, the global supply chains were thrown into total disarray. The traders panic when the rhythm changes. If the Saudis want to stabilize supply, they should probably just send me a more consistent brand of sugar, because my current supply is making the price of Brent Crude look like a rollercoaster.

Q: How do you respond to professional economists who say this defies all logic of commodity trading?

A: Those economists haven't had a proper cutting-chai during a market crash. They think it's all about geopolitical supply chain logistics, but they are just missing the fact that my wrist fatigue is the primary driver of international inflation.
caption: Forget the markets—the real power move is the morning caffeine cycle. The secret to global stability was in our kettles all along. ☕️🛢️ #OilPrices #GlobalEconomy #ChaiLife (satire)
